intended_object: The map sending a nonempty subset S of the index set to the quadratic subfield K(∏_{i∈S} √d_i) of the multiquadratic field M = K(√d_i : i). It is defined under the hypothesis that the d_i are independent in K^×/K^{×2}, so that this subfield has degree 2. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition sends a nonempty S to the intermediate field `adjoin K {∏_{i∈S} root i}`, built inside M = `adjoin K (Set.range root)`. It also packages the proof that this field has degree 2 over K. That proof uses `hroot` (each root i squares to d i) and the fact that ∏_{i∈S} d_i is not a square, which `hindep` supplies.

This matches the textbook construction exactly: under square-class independence, each nonempty subset gives the quadratic subfield K(√(∏_{i∈S} d_i)).

The generality is natural. K and L are arbitrary fields, ι is an arbitrary index type, and no characteristic assumption is imposed here; `NeZero 2` is only needed later, for injectivity. One could weaken `hindep` to "∏_{i∈S} d_i is not a square for this particular S", but the family-wide assumption is the standard setting and does not change the object.

Mathlib has no counterpart for multiquadratic fields or this subset-to-subfield map.
